title: Basic Category Theory for Computer Scientists
note: Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: A compact first course in category theory aimed at programming-language researchers. The first chapter builds the vocabulary from examples in sets, posets and type systems: diagrams, special arrows, initial and terminal objects, products, equalizers, pullbacks, general limits and exponentials. The second adds functors, F-algebras (the categorical view of datatypes and folds), natural transformations and adjunctions. The third shows the payoff in computer science: cartesian closed categories as models of the typed lambda calculus, implicit coercions and generic operators, semantics of programming languages, and solving recursive domain equations. A last chapter is an annotated guide to further reading.
